target_customer: Bloggers and publishers who wanted a hosted comment system, later advertisers via an ad network
problem: Blog comments were siloed and hard to manage. Disqus gave sites a drop-in threaded comment system with a portable identity.
business_model: free embedded comments monetized by advertising and premium plans

founders.name: Daniel Ha
founders.background_notes: Per search coverage, Ha and Jason Yan met in 7th grade and started Disqus while studying at UC Davis.

competitors.name: IntenseDebate
competitors.traction_then: public beta launched the same day as Disqus, 2007-10-30

competitors.name: JS-Kit
competitors.traction_then: vendor claim of 20 million impressions per day

technical_complexity.rationale: Hosted threaded comments with identity across many sites needed scalable infrastructure but was standard web engineering.

defensibility.rationale: A shared identity and the comment history on millions of sites created lock-in, though other comment systems were similar.

takeover_risk_then.outcome: Facebook and others launched competing comment plugins later, but Disqus reported over 4 million sites on the YC page and sold to Zeta Global in December 2017.

market_need_then: Third-party comment systems were a crowded and discussed category in 2007 as bloggers wanted richer comment features and identity.

branding.name_origin: Ha told ReadWrite he picked the name by typing letters in Photoshop to see their shapes; an invented word with a free .com.
branding.domain_note: disqus.com was available as a .com per Ha.

identity.logo: Logo mattered to Ha from the start; a 2017 interview says most installs came from people clicking the Disqus logo

branding.brand_signature: The embedded Disqus logo link on millions of comment sections
branding.community_and_virality: The widget logo drove installs and awareness across sites; Ha publicly said he disliked the name.

brand_strength.rationale: Logo exposure across millions of sites drove installs per a 2017 Ha interview, though the founder himself criticized the name.

pivots.to: forked into two products with a revamped real-time comment system
pivots.why: TechCrunch reports Disqus forked into two products in August 2009; reason not sourced.

outcome_analysis: Disqus launched in October 2007 into a crowded field of comment systems, raised a half million in 2008 and a 10 million round in 2011, and spread through an embedded logo on over 4 million sites. Zeta Global bought it in December 2017 for a reported 90 million dollars, after a 2017 breach, and a later Norwegian privacy penalty proposal followed.
notes: Series B label for the 10M May 2011 round varies by aggregator (Seedtable calls it Series C); total raised estimates 10.5M to 11.5M. YC page gives no founder education; UC Davis comes from search coverage of Wikipedia and interviews and was not opened directly. The 90M price is from SiliconANGLE; another source says undisclosed. Norway DPA intended 2.5M euro fine in 2021, final outcome not confirmed. UC Davis study detail appears only in unopened search snippets and is not recorded as education.
